transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use it again until a qualified engineer has checked it. Burning-rubber smell with the brush stopped points to the brush-drive area overheating: most often a roller jammed with hair/thread or a slipping/damaged belt; less often the floorhead’s brush motor has failed. The hose suction being OK makes the main suction motor less likely. With it switched off and unplugged only:
1. Turn the floorhead over. Remove hair and thread from around the roller and especially its end caps. Try turning the roller by hand. It should turn freely; if stiff or seized, that supports a jammed/worn roller.
2. If the base plate can be removed using its normal catches/screws, look at the rubber drive belt. A snapped, displaced, glazed or loose belt supports a belt fault.
3. Look for melted plastic, black rubber dust, or heat damage around the roller/belt area. That supports overheating and is another reason not to run it. These checks can identify the failed area, but they do not make the vacuum safe to put back into service after a burning smell. If the roller and belt look intact, the brush-bar motor or its wiring in the floorhead is the more likely fault and needs an engineer.

ok its unplugged n i turned it over. roller was tight, loads of hair n a tassel wrapped round the ends. cut it all off and it spins free by hand now. took the cover off and the belt is snapped in 2 bits, one bit has a shiny melted looking edge. no sparks or electrical smell, just the rubber smell right when it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The jammed roller has very likely overloaded the brush drive and caused the belt to overheat and snap. Do not run it again, including after fitting anything, as it needs a qualified engineer to assess it following the burning smell. With it still unplugged, only inspect the roller end caps and the belt-drive/pulley area for melted or distorted plastic, blackening, or built-up rubber debris. If any is present, that supports damage beyond the belt itself. If it all looks clean and intact, the belt is still the main failed component, with the hair/tassel jam as the likely cause.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
This points very strongly to the brush-drive belt snapping after the hair and tassel jammed the roller. Do not use the vacuum again, even with a replacement belt fitted, until a qualified engineer has checked it because of the burning smell. ⚠ Stop using this appliance
U85-AS-BE is a Vax Air Stretch model reference, but it does not change the diagnosis: the failed part is most likely the brush-drive belt. The hair and tassel jammed the roller, and the resistance overheated the belt until it melted and snapped. The freely turning roller and sound end caps make a failed roller less likely. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it because of the burning smell. The one remaining useful check is the belt-drive pulley/spindle: with it unplugged, look for melted or distorted plastic, black rubber deposits, or a pulley that looks damaged. Any of those means the drive area has been heat-damaged, not just the belt. If that area looks clean and undamaged, the evidence still strongly supports the belt as the main failed component, with the cleared tangle as the cause. An engineer can confirm the pulley and brush drive are sound before fitting the correct belt.
